with $c_1\,:=\,\rho(1-\beta)^2$ and some constant $C_1$. Taking conditional expectation in (25) and using the above bound, we obtain

$$ \begin{align*}\mathbb{E}[\bar{L}_{k}(\Omega_{k+1})\mid\mathcal{F}_{k}]\leq\bar{L}_{k}(\Omega_{k})-\eta_{k}\Big(\frac{1-\beta}{2}-\frac{c_{1}}{2(1-\beta)}\Big)\|g_{k}\|^{2}\\+\frac{\eta_{k}\beta^{2}}{2(1-\beta)}\|v_{k}\|^{2}-A_{k}\mathbb{E}[\|v_{k+1}\|^{2}\mid\mathcal{F}_{k}]\\+C_{2}\eta_{k}(\delta_{k}+\sigma_{k}^{2})\end{align*} $$

for some constant $C_2$ and $A_k := \frac{\eta_k}{2(1-\beta)} - \frac{M_k \eta_k^2}{2} - \frac{\eta_k \varepsilon}{2(1-\beta）。$

Choosing $\rho \in (0,1)$ and defining $c_2 := \frac{1-\beta}{2}(1-\rho) > 0$,

(27) becomes

$$ \begin{align*}\mathbb{E}[\bar{L}_{k}(\Omega_{k+1})\mid\mathcal{F}_{k}]\leq\bar{L}_{k}(\Omega_{k})-c_{2}\eta_{k}\|g_{k}\|^{2}+\frac{\eta_{k}\beta^{2}}{2(1-\beta)}\|v_{k}\|^{2}\\-A_{k}\mathbb{E}[\|v_{k+1}\|^{2}\mid\mathcal{F}_{k}]+C_{2}^{\prime}\eta_{k}(\delta_{k}+\sigma_{k}^{2}).\end{align*} $$
for some constant  $ C_{2}^{\prime} $. Define the Lyapunov function
$$ \Phi_{k}:=\bar{L}_{k}(\Omega_{k})+\lambda_{k}\|v_{k}\|^{2},\qquad\lambda_{k}:=\frac{\eta_{k}\beta^{2}}{2(1-\beta)}. $$
Using the drift condition  $ \bar{L}_{k+1}(\Omega_{k+1}) \leq \bar{L}_k(\Omega_{k+1}) + \bar{d}_k $ together with (28), we obtain

$$ \begin{align*}\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{k+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_{k}]\leq\Phi_{k}-c_{2}\eta_{k}\|g_{k}\|^{2}+\bar{d}_{k}+C_{2}^{\prime}\eta_{k}(\delta_{k}+\sigma_{k}^{2})\\-\Big(A_{k}-\lambda_{k+1}\Big)\mathbb{E}[\|v_{k+1}\|^{2}\mid\mathcal{F}_{k}].\end{align*} $$
Since  $ \eta_k $ is nonincreasing and  $ \lambda_{k+1} \leq \eta_k \beta^2 / [2(1 - \beta)] $,

$$ \begin{align*}A_{k}-\lambda_{k+1}&=\frac{\eta_{k}}{2(1-\beta)}-\frac{M_{k}\eta_{k}^{2}}{2}-\frac{\eta_{k}\varepsilon}{2(1-\beta)}-\lambda_{k+1}\\&\geq\eta_{k}\Big(\frac{1+\beta}{2}-\frac{\varepsilon}{2(1-\beta)}-\frac{M_{k}\eta_{k}}{2}\Big).\end{align*} $$

Choose  $ \varepsilon > 0 $ sufficiently small such that  $ \frac{1+\beta}{2} - \frac{\varepsilon}{2(1-\beta)} > 0 $. Since  $ \eta_k M_k \to 0 $, there exist  $ k_0 $ and  $ c_3 > 0 $ such that the coefficient in (30) is at least  $ c_3 \eta_k $ for all  $ k \geq k_0 $. Hence the last term in (29) is nonpositive for all sufficiently large  $ k $, and thus for  $ k \geq k_0 $,
$$ \begin{array}{r}{\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{k+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_{k}]\leq\Phi_{k}-c_{2}\eta_{k}\|g_{k}\|^{2}+\bar{d}_{k}+C_{2}^{\prime}\eta_{k}(\delta_{k}+\sigma_{k}^{2}).}\end{array} $$
Taking full expectation and summing (31) from  $ k_{0} $ to K gives

$$ \begin{align*}\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{K+1}]\leq\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{k_{0}}]-c_{2}\sum_{k=k_{0}}^{K}\eta_{k}\mathbb{E}[\|g_{k}\|^{2}]+\sum_{k=k_{0}}^{K}\bar{d}_{k}\\+C_{2}^{\prime}\sum_{k=k_{0}}^{K}\eta_{k}(\delta_{k}+\sigma_{k}^{2}).\end{align*} $$
Since  $ \bar{L}_k(\Omega_k) \geq 0 $ and  $ \lambda_k \|v_k\|^2 \geq 0 $, we have  $ \Phi_k \geq 0 $. Using Assumption 2 and letting  $ K \to \infty $ in (32), we conclude that
$$ \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_{k}\mathbb{E}[\left\|g_{k}\right\|^{2}]<\infty. $$
$$ \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_{k}\mathbb{E}\big[\|\nabla\bar{L}_{k}(\Omega_{k})\|^{2}\big]<\infty. $$
Equivalently,
Notice that  $ \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_{k}=\infty $ by Assumption 3, it follows that
$$ \liminf_{k\to\infty}\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla\bar{L}_{k}(\Omega_{k})\|^{2}]=0. $$
This completes the proof.
